cohort: The study included 108 participants, comprising 54 children diagnosed with Transient Hypogammaglobulinemia of Infancy (THI) and 54 normoglobulinemic healthy control children.
finding: Multiple factors, including male sex, cesarean section birth, low parental education, various medication uses during pregnancy, gestational diabetes/preeclampsia, smoking exposure, atopic conditions, low socioeconomic level, and breastfeeding for less than 6 months, were significantly associated with the occurrence of Transient Hypogammaglobulinemia of Infancy (THI).
mod_finding: Cesarean section birth was found to be significantly associated with Transient Hypogammaglobulinemia of Infancy (p = 0.003).
